points.description: Says that removing each electron leaves fewer electrons, so there is less electron-electron repulsion, and links this to lower potential energy (the remaining electrons are held more tightly / are more stable). An implied link is enough.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only decreased electron-electron repulsion is stated, with no link to potential energy

points.description: The 3rd and 4th electrons come from the same shell (n=3), so they have about the same radius and feel the same core charge. This is why their ionization energies (3231 and 4356) are similar and fairly close.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only same shell/radius or only same core charge is stated

points.description: The 5th electron comes from an inner shell (n=2), so it has a smaller radius and feels a higher core charge. This gives a much larger ionization energy (16091).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only the inner shell/smaller radius or only the higher core charge is stated

points.description: Explains with Coulomb's law that stronger attraction (higher core charge, smaller distance) means lower potential energy for the electron, so more energy is needed to remove it. That is, higher ionization energy goes with lower potential energy.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only partly stated, e.g. stronger attraction means more energy is needed, with no link to potential energy

rubric.notes: Full marks need the four ideas in any wording: less repulsion lowers potential energy, 3rd and 4th electrons are in the same shell with the same core charge and radius, the 5th is in an inner shell with higher core charge and smaller radius, and lower potential energy means higher ionization energy. Give part marks for answers that are on the right track but vague or incomplete, and accept implied links. Restating the question or wrong extra remarks cost nothing unless they contradict the central idea.
